question: A manager spends 12 hours preparing four lectures for 10 staff. Why did Andy Grove think it time well spent?
answer: Because of leverage, a little of one person’s time multiplied across many. In Grove’s sums, those 10 people will work about 20,000 hours over the next year, so a course that makes them just 1% better returns some 200 hours of work for the manager’s 12.
move: Count time spent teaching against every hour your learners will then work.
simply: Spend one afternoon teaching your little brother to tie his shoes, and you save every morning you’d have spent tying them for him. One afternoon, hundreds of mornings.
why: It changes how to judge time spent explaining things, at work or at home. Showing a colleague a shortcut, or a child how to do a chore, costs an hour now and pays back every time they do it without you.
